note: Track intervals-on-neck (guitar-scales), step 2, on guitar-play-along's interval shape: the 5ths of a major key on the low E and A strings, then its 4ths on the same strings, then both in turn on the A and D strings. Each walk runs up the neck low note first and back down high note first. The why gives the two shapes and says one pair of each is a fret off, so the odd one is expected; the tab shows the frets. It states its moves (any key, tempo 60 to 90) and mentions no selector.

exercise.title: 5ths and 4ths on the next string in {{=key}} major
exercise.why: On the next string a 4th sits in the same fret and a 5th two frets higher, so the two shapes are one finger apart; in every key one pair of each is a fret off, and knowing that keeps your hand from guessing.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the backing track at {{=bpm}}, and play along from the tab: a note on the low E string, then the note a 5th above it on the A string. The pairs climb the neck low note first, then come back down high note first.
Most of the 5ths have one shape and one is a fret narrower: play until your hand goes to that one without stopping.

Press Play below to start the backing track. Now each pair is a 4th: most sit in one fret across the two strings, and one is a fret wider.
If a pair sounds wrong, stop the backing track and find it in the tab before you start again.

Press Play below to start the backing track. The 5ths come first and the 4ths start on a new bar, now on the A and D strings. The line above the tab says which is playing.
In another key the pairs sit on other frets, and the two shapes stay as they were.
